text.title: test-fixtures Failure Modes
text.summary: 7 antipatterns specific to test-fixtures. Each has a description, an observable detector and a concrete repair.

failure-mode.description: `scope="module"` or `scope="session"` fixtures yield mutable state; one test mutates it, later tests inherit it. Symptom: tests pass alone, fail in suite.
failure-mode.detector: `pytest tests/test_x.py::test_y` passes while the full run fails; `fixture-pollution-check.sh` fails under some seeds and not others; a fixture with wider scope yields a list, dict, ORM session or model instance.
failure-mode.repair: Return to `scope="function"`; profile with `pytest --durations=20` before widening again, and widen only fixtures whose object is immutable. Rules r-function-scope-default, r-order-independence-gate.

failure-mode.description: Teardown code is not idempotent, or two fixtures share a resource and depend on finalizer order, so a failing test raises a second exception from cleanup that masks the original, or cleanup of one fixture breaks the other.
failure-mode.detector: Traceback shows "During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred" originating after `yield`; a fixture's teardown references an object owned by another fixture; the suite passes only when fixture parameters are listed in one specific order.
failure-mode.repair: Make each fixture release only what it acquired, guard teardown so a second run is a no-op, and use `request.addfinalizer` when one fixture must register cleanup for another. Rule r-yield-cleanup.

failure-mode.description: `make_user()` defaults change and the implicit assumptions of 200 tests change with them; failures appear in tests that never mention the changed field.
failure-mode.detector: A factory diff touches a default value and the CI failure set includes tests that do not pass that field; a factory has positional parameters; two modules define their own `make_user`.
failure-mode.repair: One factory per entity, keyword-only parameters, explicit defaults; grep callers before changing a default and pass the old value explicitly where a test depended on it. Rule r-keyword-only-factories.

failure-mode.description: `db_session` lives in the root `conftest.py` and is imported or requested everywhere, so switching SQLAlchemy sync to async, or swapping the ORM, breaks every fixture transitively.
failure-mode.detector: Root `conftest.py` imports `sqlalchemy` / `django.db` directly; test modules import fixtures with `from tests.conftest import ...`; more than one conftest defines a `db_session`.
failure-mode.repair: Move ORM-specific fixtures to their own module registered via `pytest_plugins`; keep the root conftest to cross-package fixtures only. Rule r-conftest-layering.

failure-mode.description: `autouse=True` on a database or network fixture runs it for every test, including pure-function tests; wall time balloons and no test signature explains why.
failure-mode.detector: `pytest --durations=20` lists a fixture setup for tests that do not name it; total suite time scales with test count rather than with the number of DB tests.
failure-mode.repair: Remove `autouse` from any fixture doing I/O; request it by name where needed. Rule r-no-autouse-io.

failure-mode.description: `faker.email()`, `random.choice()` or `datetime.now()` in a factory default produces a different value each run; snapshot and ordering assertions flake.
failure-mode.detector: A snapshot diff shows only generated values changing; the same test alternates pass/fail with no code change; `Faker.seed()` or `pytest-randomly` is absent from the suite.
failure-mode.repair: Use a per-run sequence for any asserted field; seed faker once; keep faker for fields no assertion reads. Rule r-sequenced-determinism.

failure-mode.description: Under `pytest-xdist` a `session`-scoped fixture is assumed to run once for the whole run; in reality it runs once per worker, and workers collide on the same database name or seed the same rows in parallel.
failure-mode.detector: Failures appear only with `-n auto`; errors are duplicate-key, "database already exists" or "already seeded" checks stored in module globals; the fixture never reads `worker_id`.
failure-mode.repair: Name worker-private resources with `worker_id`, or guard a shared build with the file-lock recipe from the pytest-xdist docs. Rule r-xdist-per-worker-state.
